title: Delete stale rule .done markers when extending a Snakemake pipeline's scope mid-project
summary: In individual-rule submission mode, targeting a rule-name aggregator can report 'Nothing to be done' even though new work (e.g. a newly added region/chromosome/sample) is required, if a .done marker from an earlier narrower run still exists. Verify by targeting the exact new output file directly; if that path triggers work but the aggregator doesn't, delete the stale .done marker files to force Snakemake to re-examine the full dependency list.
trigger: adding new regions/chromosomes/samples to an already-completed Snakemake pipeline and getting an unexpected 'Nothing to be done'

title: `module load X 2>/dev/null || true` can silently no-op inside a non-interactive sbatch script
summary: Suppressing module-load errors with `|| true` hides the fact that the `module` command itself may not be initialized in a non-interactive SLURM job shell, leaving the wrong (or a bare default) toolchain on PATH with no visible failure. If a script depends on a specific interpreter/toolchain, resolve and export its absolute bin path directly instead of trusting `module load` to have worked.
trigger: writing an sbatch script that calls module load before running an interpreter or tool, especially if failures are silenced

title: `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1` can cause a false ModuleNotFoundError for a package that IS installed
summary: If a package was installed with `pip install --user`, setting PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 hides it from the interpreter even when PATH and the module/toolchain are otherwise correct -- the resulting ImportError looks like a missing dependency, not an environment-variable problem. Check for this env var specifically when an import fails despite pip show/pip list confirming the package is present.
trigger: debugging a ModuleNotFoundError in a non-interactive job shell for a package pip confirms is installed

title: Pick genotype-merge strategy (union vs. intersection) by what the downstream tool tolerates, not by habit
summary: When merging multiple genotyped cohorts into one panel, an intersection (common-SNP-only) merge gives near-zero missingness but can be too sparse for tools that need positional SNP density (e.g. an LD/fine-mapping reference panel needing a minimum match rate). Use a union merge instead when the consumer mode-imputes missing calls (e.g. bigsnpr's snp_fastImputeSimple). Conversely, use an intersection merge for GRM/heritability estimation, where dense non-imputed genotypes are wanted rather than tolerating imputed missingness.

title: Bumping a Snakemake rule's cluster time-limit isn't enough if the orchestrating sbatch controller has its own, smaller --time budget
summary: When a cluster job hits its SLURM time limit, increasing just the rule's resources.time (or a job's requested time) can still fail silently if the outer controller/orchestrator script that submits and waits on it has its own shorter --time in its own #SBATCH header -- the controller gets killed and the dispatched sub-job is orphaned before it can finish, even though the actual computation would have completed given more time. Always check and align BOTH budgets (the rule/job AND its orchestrator) when responding to a timeout, not just the one that actually got killed.
trigger: increasing a rule's or job's SLURM time resource after a timeout, when that job is itself launched by another sbatch/controller script
